_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Pakistan covering Indus Valley Civilization, Indo-Greeks, Buddhist Gandhara, Delhi Sultanate, Mughal Empire, British Raj, partition of India 1947 (largest mass migration in history, ~2M dead), Kashmir conflict, military coups (Ayub, Zia, Musharraf), Bangladesh independence 1971, Islamisation under Zia, nuclear weapons 1998, Taliban/Al-Qaeda presence, drone war, and civilian-military power struggles.

religion.note: Islamic Republic; Islam state religion since 1956; blasphemy laws (death penalty for insulting Prophet); Ahmadis declared 'non-Muslim' 1974 (persecuted); Sunni-Shia sectarian violence; Deobandi/Barelvi divide; Sufi shrines (Data Darbar, Sehwan Sharif); TTP/TLP Islamist groups

ethnic_groups.name: Punjabi
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest group; dominant politically/militarily; fertile plains; Lahore cultural capital; Urdu and Punjabi speakers; control establishment

ethnic_groups.name: Pashtun (Pathan)
ethnic_groups.notes: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa + FATA; cross-border with Afghanistan; Pashto; tribal (Pakhtunwali code); Taliban support base; Imran Khan has Pashtun heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Sindhi
ethnic_groups.notes: Sindh province; Urdu-speaking Mohajir vs indigenous Sindhi tension; PPP support base (Bhutto family); Karachi divided demographics

ethnic_groups.name: Saraiki
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Punjab; distinct from Punjabi; movement for separate province; marginalized

ethnic_groups.name: Mohajir/Urdu-speaking
ethnic_groups.notes: 1947 Partition migrants from India; Urdu mother tongue; urban Sindh (Karachi/Hyderabad); MQM party; middle-class; 'stranded Pakistanis'

ethnic_groups.name: Baloch
ethnic_groups.notes: Balochistan (largest province by area, smallest by population); tribal; insurgency since 1948 (BLA, BLF); natural gas exploitation grievances; poorest province; cross-border with Iran/Afghanistan

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Hindko, Brahui, Hazara, Kalash, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: Hazara (Shia, persecuted, Quetta); Kalash (animist, Chitral, ~4,000); Brahui (Balochistan); numerous smaller groups

country_profile.notes_unique: Only Muslim-majority nuclear weapons state; 1947 Partition (~2M dead, 15M displaced); Kashmir conflict with India (3 wars); East Pakistan became Bangladesh 1971 (~3M dead); military has ruled ~33 of 77 years (coups 1958, 1977, 1999); ISI intelligence agency; Osama bin Laden killed in Abbottabad 2011; TTP/Taliban presence; Durand Line (Afghanistan border dispute); K2 (Karakoram, world's 2nd highest peak); Indus River; CPEC (China-Pakistan Economic Corridor)

trade.notes: Textiles 60%+ of exports; rice 2nd largest exporter; CPEC trade infrastructure; GSP+ EU trade preferences; low trade openness for large economy; textile value chain critical.

infrastructure.notes: CPEC transformative ($62B); Gwadar port (Chinese-operated); Karakoram Highway; M-tag motorway system; chronic electricity load shedding; colonial-era railway; Lahore Orange Line metro.

governance_indices.notes: Military establishment dominant; 2022 political crisis (Imran Khan ouster/arrest); civilian-military hybrid governance; feudal politics; judiciary independence contested.

geography.terrain: Flat Indus River plain east; Balochistan plateau west; northern mountains (Karakoram, Hindu Kush, Himalayas); Thar Desert southeast
geography.notes: K2 world's 2nd highest peak; Indus River civilization origin; nuclear weapons state; Karakoram Highway world's highest paved road; 2022 floods inundated 1/3 of country.

economy_extended.notes: Chronic balance of payments crises; 24th IMF program (2023 SBA); circular debt; CPEC ($62B Chinese investment); textiles dominant manufacturing; informal economy 30%+; 2022 floods $30B damage.

health.notes: Polio-endemic (one of two countries); high stunting/malnutrition; lady health worker program; private sector dominant; Sehat Sahulat health card program; TB third highest globally.

food_agriculture.notes: Indus basin irrigation world's largest contiguous; wheat self-sufficient most years; cotton 4th globally; mango exporter; 2022 floods destroyed 50%+ crops; water scarcity increasing.

security_stability.notes: Nuclear weapons state; Kashmir conflict with India; TTP resurgence post-Taliban Afghanistan; world's largest refugee host (Afghan); military vs. civilian power dynamic; CPEC security challenges.

environment_climate.notes: 2022 super-floods (1/3 country underwater); $30B+ damage; Billion Tree Tsunami reforestation; melting glaciers threatening water supply; air quality among world's worst; climate-vulnerable.

demographics_extended.notes: World's 5th most populous (240M+); very young; Punjabi 45%, Pashtun 15%, Sindhi 14%, Muhajir 8%; 22M out-of-school children; madrasa education system parallel; gender gap 2nd worst globally.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Nuclear-armed; world's 5th most populous; cricket superpower; complex security environment; CPEC (China–Pakistan Economic Corridor).

music_art_traditions: Qawwali (Sufi devotional, Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan)
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: Dawn, The News (English); Jang, Express (Urdu); Geo TV, ARY News, Dawn News; vibrant but pressured media landscape.
cultural_heritage.notes: Indus Valley (Mohenjo-daro, Harappa); Mughal heritage; Sufi tradition; 6 UNESCO sites; truck art unique; cricket passion; diverse provinces.

energy.notes: CPEC energy projects; circular debt crisis; loadshedding chronic; Tarbela and Mangla dams; nuclear plants (Chashma, Karachi); LNG imports growing; solar boom.

human_rights_gender.notes: Honour killings persist; blasphemy law (Section 295-C, death penalty); enforced disappearances (Balochistan); military influence in politics; trans rights (2018 law, unique).

legal_system.legal_tradition: English common law with Islamic law (Sharia) provisions
legal_system.sharia_applicability: Objective Resolution; Federal Shariat Court reviews laws for Islamic compliance; Hudood Ordinances
legal_system.notes: Supreme Court; Federal Shariat Court; dual civil-Islamic system; 18th Amendment (2010) devolved powers; military courts (controversial); FATA merger (2018).

tourism.notes: Tourism potential massive; security improvements in north; K2 and Karakoram; Gandhara Buddhist heritage; Mughal architecture; e-visa launched.

transport.notes: Pakistan Railways (colonial-era network); Karakoram Highway (China link); CPEC infrastructure boom; Gwadar deep-water port; PIA (national airline, privatisation planned).

current_leader.name: Asif Ali Zardari
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: PPP; second term (also 2008-13); widower of Benazir Bhutto; 'Mr. 10%' corruption allegations; ceremonial role

prime_minister.name: Shehbaz Sharif
prime_minister.title: Prime Minister
prime_minister.notes: PML-N; brother of Nawaz Sharif; second term (also 2022-23); executive power; ousted Imran Khan

former_leaders.name: Imran Khan
former_leaders.notes: PTI; cricket legend (1992 World Cup); populist; military-backed rise; ousted by no-confidence (2022); arrested May 2023 (dozens of charges, corruption/sedition); huge support base; marriage to Jemima Khan

former_leaders.name: Nawaz Sharif
former_leaders.notes: PML-N; three-time PM; industrial magnate; removed by Supreme Court 2017 (Panama Papers); exiled/jailed then returned; military tensions

former_leaders.name: Benazir Bhutto
former_leaders.notes: PPP; first female PM of Muslim-majority country; daughter of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto; assassinated December 2007 (suicide bomb); corruption charges in exile; returned for 2008 election

former_leaders.name: Pervez Musharraf
former_leaders.notes: General; military coup 1999 (ousted Nawaz Sharif); President; allied with US in War on Terror; Lal Masjid siege 2007; resigned under impeachment threat; died 2023 in exile

former_leaders.name: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
former_leaders.notes: PPP founder; populist socialist; 1971 Bangladesh war; Ahmadi persecution; executed by Zia (1979) on murder charges; Bhutto dynasty founder

former_leaders.name: Yahya Khan
former_leaders.notes: General; President; 1971 Bangladesh genocide/war; resigned in disgrace

former_leaders.name: Ayub Khan
former_leaders.notes: General; first military coup (1958); 1965 war with India; resigned after protests

former_leaders.name: Muhammad Ali Jinnah
former_leaders.notes: Founder of Pakistan ('Quaid-e-Azam'); Muslim League; two-nation theory; Governor-General; died 1948 (TB)

910.name: Indus Valley and Gandhara Civilizations
910.description: The great Indus Valley Civilization centered on Mohenjo-daro and Harappa in Pakistan, followed by the Indo-Aryan Vedic expansion, and the rise of Gandhara as a Mahajanapada in the northwestern frontier.

sub_clusters.name: Harappan Civilization
sub_clusters.description: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa as the twin capitals of the Indus Valley Civilization, the Great Bath, the Dancing Girl, the undeciphered Indus script, and the civilization's sophisticated urban planning.
key_events: Mohenjo-daro flourishes as one of the world's earliest great cities with advanced drainage systems (c. 2500 BC)
Harappa thrives as a major trade center with standardized weights and measures

sub_clusters.name: Vedic and Gandharan Period
sub_clusters.description: The Indo-Aryan settlement of the Punjab, the Gandhara Mahajanapada centered on Taxila, the composition of Vedic hymns in the Land of Seven Rivers, and the development of Taxila as a great learning center.

910.name: Achaemenid, Greek, and Mauryan Period
910.description: Darius I's incorporation of the Indus region into the Persian Empire, Alexander the Great's invasion of the Punjab, the Maurya Empire under Chandragupta and Ashoka, and Taxila as a world center of learning.

sub_clusters.name: Persian and Alexandrian Period
sub_clusters.description: Darius I's conquest of the Indus Valley as Achaemenid satrapies, Alexander the Great's epic Battle of the Hydaspes against King Porus, and the Hellenistic influence at Taxila.
key_events: Alexander the Great defeats King Porus at the Battle of the Hydaspes on the Jhelum River (326 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Mauryan and Ashoka Period
sub_clusters.description: Chandragupta Maurya's recovery of the Indus region from Seleucus, Ashoka's rule and Buddhist edicts at Mansehra and Shahbazgarhi, and Taxila as the Maurya Empire's northwestern capital.
key_events: Ashoka's Rock Edicts carved at Mansehra and Shahbazgarhi in Pakistan (c. 260 BC)

910.name: Indo-Greek, Kushan, and Gandharan Art
910.description: The Indo-Greek kingdoms of the Punjab, the Kushan Empire's Silk Road grandeur, and the flowering of Gandharan Greco-Buddhist art — one of the most remarkable artistic traditions in world history.

sub_clusters.name: Indo-Greek and Indo-Scythian Kingdoms
sub_clusters.description: The Indo-Greek kings of the Punjab including the famous Menander I (Milinda), the Milinda Panha philosophical dialogue, and the subsequent Indo-Scythian and Indo-Parthian rule.

sub_clusters.name: Kushan Empire and Gandharan Zenith
sub_clusters.description: The Kushan Empire under Kanishka with its capital near Peshawar, the creation of the first human images of the Buddha in Gandharan art, the fusion of Greek, Roman, Indian, and Central Asian styles, and the Silk Road wealth.
key_events: Gandharan sculptors create the first anthropomorphic images of the Buddha, revolutionizing Buddhist art
Kanishka's great stupa at Purushapura (Peshawar) becomes one of the tallest structures in the ancient world

sub_clusters.name: Gupta and White Hun Period
sub_clusters.description: The Gupta influence in eastern Punjab, the devastating Hephthalite (White Hun) invasions that destroyed many Gandharan Buddhist sites, and the decline of Buddhism in the region.

920.name: Arab Conquest and Early Muslim Period
920.description: Muhammad bin Qasim's Arab conquest of Sindh, the Ghaznavid and Ghurid invasions through the mountain passes, and the establishment of Muslim political power in the subcontinent via Pakistani territory.

sub_clusters.name: Arab Conquest of Sindh
sub_clusters.description: Muhammad bin Qasim's conquest of Sindh and Multan — the first permanent Muslim foothold in the subcontinent, the Chach Nama chronicle, and the development of Indo-Muslim culture in Sindh.
key_events: Muhammad bin Qasim conquers Sindh, establishing the first Muslim territory in the subcontinent (711 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Ghaznavid and Ghurid Invasions
sub_clusters.description: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni's raids through the Punjab, Lahore as the Ghaznavid eastern capital, the Ghurid conquests, and Pakistan's territory as the gateway for Muslim power into India.
key_events: Lahore becomes the eastern capital of the Ghaznavid Empire under Mahmud (c. 1021 AD)
Data Ganj Bakhsh (Ali Hujwiri) writes Kashf al-Mahjub, the oldest Persian treatise on Sufism, at Lahore (c. 1070 AD)

920.name: Delhi Sultanate Rule and Sufi Heritage
920.description: The Punjab and Sindh under Delhi Sultanate rule, the extraordinary flowering of Sufi culture and shrines, the poetry of Shah Hussain and Bulleh Shah's predecessors, and the Langah and Samma sultanates.

sub_clusters.name: Sultanate Provinces and Regional Powers
sub_clusters.description: The Punjab under successive Delhi Sultanate dynasties, the independent Samma dynasty of Sindh, the Langah Sultanate of Multan, Timur's devastation of the Punjab, and the rich Sufi shrine culture.

sub_clusters.name: Sufi Saints and Cultural Fusion
sub_clusters.description: The great Sufi saints of Pakistan — Data Ganj Bakhsh, Baha ud-Din Zakariya, Shah Rukn-e-Alam, and Lal Shahbaz Qalandar — whose shrines remain the most revered sites in Pakistani Islam.
key_events: Lal Shahbaz Qalandar's shrine at Sehwan Sharif becomes one of the holiest Sufi sites in the subcontinent (c. 1274)

930.name: Mughal Pakistan
930.description: The Punjab and Sindh as heartlands of the Mughal Empire, Lahore as a magnificent imperial capital, the Sikh-Mughal conflicts, and the post-Mughal fragmentation.

sub_clusters.name: Mughal Lahore and Punjab
sub_clusters.description: Lahore as one of the great Mughal imperial cities, the Shalimar Gardens, the Badshahi Mosque, Akbar's fort at Lahore, the Grand Trunk Road, and the Punjab as the breadbasket of the empire.
key_events: Akbar builds the magnificent Lahore Fort and makes Lahore a Mughal capital (1584–1598)
Aurangzeb builds the Badshahi Mosque, one of the largest mosques in the world (1673)

sub_clusters.name: Sikh Rise and Durrani Influence
sub_clusters.description: The post-Mughal chaos in the Punjab, Ahmad Shah Durrani's invasions from Afghanistan, the rise of Sikh misls (confederacies), and the contest for control of Lahore and the Punjab.
key_events: Ahmad Shah Durrani sacks Delhi and controls Punjab and Kashmir (1757–1761)

930.name: Sikh Empire and British Conquest
930.description: Maharaja Ranjit Singh's powerful Sikh Empire in the Punjab, the Anglo-Sikh Wars, the British conquest, and the annexation of Sindh and the frontier regions.

sub_clusters.name: Ranjit Singh's Sikh Empire
sub_clusters.description: Maharaja Ranjit Singh's creation of the powerful Sikh Empire from Lahore, the modernized Khalsa Army, the Koh-i-Noor diamond, and the Anglo-Sikh Wars ending in British annexation of the Punjab.
key_events: Maharaja Ranjit Singh unifies the Punjab under the Sikh Empire (1799–1839)
Second Anglo-Sikh War — Britain annexes the Punjab after the Battle of Gujrat (1849)

sub_clusters.name: Sindh and Frontier Annexation
sub_clusters.description: Sir Charles Napier's controversial conquest of Sindh ('Peccavi'), the subjugation of Balochistan and the tribal frontier, and the 1857 Rebellion in the regions of modern Pakistan.
key_events: British annex Sindh after defeating the Talpur Mirs at the Battle of Miani (1843)

940.name: British Raj and Pakistan Movement
940.description: The regions of modern Pakistan under the British Raj, the growth of Muslim political consciousness, Iqbal's Allahabad Address, Jinnah's Two-Nation Theory, and the creation of Pakistan.

sub_clusters.name: Muslim Political Awakening
sub_clusters.description: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan's modernization movement, the founding of the All-India Muslim League at Dhaka, the Khilafat Movement, and Allama Iqbal's philosophical articulation of a separate Muslim homeland.
key_events: All-India Muslim League founded at Dhaka (1906)
Allama Iqbal's Allahabad Address envisions a separate Muslim state in northwestern India (1930)

sub_clusters.name: Pakistan Movement and Creation
sub_clusters.description: The Lahore Resolution demanding a separate Muslim state, Muhammad Ali Jinnah's leadership of the Muslim League, the 1946 elections, the Mountbatten Plan, and the creation of Pakistan.
key_events: Lahore Resolution — Muslim League formally demands the creation of Pakistan (23 March 1940)
Pakistan gains independence as a Muslim-majority state with two wings 1,000 miles apart (14 August 1947)

950.name: Early Pakistan and Military Rule
950.description: The traumatic birth of Pakistan, Jinnah's early death, the first military coup, Ayub Khan's modernization, the 1965 war with India, and the catastrophic loss of East Pakistan.

sub_clusters.name: Independence, Partition, and Early Crises
sub_clusters.description: The massive population exchange during Partition, Jinnah's death, the first Kashmir War, political instability, the assassination of Liaquat Ali Khan, and the first military coup by Ayub Khan.
key_events: Muhammad Ali Jinnah (Quaid-e-Azam) dies just 13 months after independence (September 1948)
First Indo-Pakistani War over Kashmir ends with a UN ceasefire line (1948–1949)

sub_clusters.name: Ayub Khan Era and 1965 War
sub_clusters.description: Field Marshal Ayub Khan's 'Decade of Development,' the new capital at Islamabad, the inconclusive 1965 war with India, the Tashkent Declaration, and the growing unrest in East Pakistan.

sub_clusters.name: 1971 War and Bangladesh Separation
sub_clusters.description: The 1970 election crisis, Operation Searchlight and the genocide in East Pakistan, the Indian military intervention, and the humiliating surrender creating Bangladesh — Pakistan losing its eastern wing.
key_events: Pakistani forces surrender in Dhaka — East Pakistan becomes Bangladesh (16 December 1971)

950.name: Bhutto and Zia Eras
950.description: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's populist democracy, Pakistan's nuclear program, Zia ul-Haq's Islamization, the Soviet-Afghan War's impact on Pakistan, and the foundations of modern Pakistan's challenges.

sub_clusters.name: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Era
sub_clusters.description: Bhutto's populist PPP government, the 1973 constitution, nationalization policies, the Simla Agreement with India, the launch of Pakistan's nuclear weapons program, and the rigged 1977 elections.
key_events: Pakistan adopts the 1973 Constitution — still the country's governing framework (1973)
Bhutto launches Pakistan's nuclear weapons program after India's 1974 test

sub_clusters.name: Zia Islamization and Afghan War
sub_clusters.description: General Zia ul-Haq's military coup and execution of Bhutto, sweeping Islamization including Hudood Ordinances, Pakistan as the frontline state in the anti-Soviet Afghan jihad, and the Ojhri Camp explosion.
key_events: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto executed after a controversial trial (April 1979)
Pakistan serves as the base for CIA-backed mujahideen during the Soviet-Afghan War (1979–1989)

960.name: Democratic Transitions and Musharraf
960.description: The alternating Bhutto-Sharif democratic governments, Pakistan's nuclear tests, Musharraf's coup, the post-9/11 alliance with the US, the War on Terror, and Benazir Bhutto's assassination.

sub_clusters.name: Bhutto-Sharif Democratic Era
sub_clusters.description: Benazir Bhutto as the Muslim world's first female prime minister, the alternating Bhutto-Sharif governments dismissed for corruption, Pakistan's nuclear tests responding to India, and the Kargil War.
key_events: Benazir Bhutto becomes the first female prime minister of a Muslim-majority nation (1988)
Pakistan conducts nuclear weapons tests at Chagai in response to India's Pokhran-II (May 1998)

sub_clusters.name: Musharraf Era and War on Terror
sub_clusters.description: General Musharraf's coup, Pakistan's post-9/11 alignment with the US, the ISI's complex relationship with the Taliban, the Lal Masjid siege, the lawyers' movement, and Benazir Bhutto's assassination.
key_events: Benazir Bhutto assassinated at a campaign rally in Rawalpindi (27 December 2007)

960.name: Contemporary Pakistan
960.description: Pakistan's turbulent democratic era, the fight against terrorism, Osama bin Laden's discovery in Abbottabad, Imran Khan's rise and fall, the economic crisis, and civil-military tensions.

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Restoration and War on Terrorism
sub_clusters.description: Zardari and Sharif governments, the military operations against the Pakistani Taliban, the Army Public School Peshawar massacre, the CPEC economic corridor, and the Panama Papers crisis.
key_events: US Navy SEALs kill Osama bin Laden in Abbottabad, Pakistan (2 May 2011)
TTP attack on Army Public School Peshawar kills 149, including 132 children (16 December 2014)

sub_clusters.name: Imran Khan Era and Political Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Imran Khan's PTI government, the no-confidence motion and removal, Khan's arrest and the May 9 protests, military establishment's political role, the economic crisis, and ongoing political polarization.
key_events: Imran Khan removed as PM through no-confidence motion; arrested in 2023 amid political crisis

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
